text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Michigan man doxxed after exposing his city's booming Islamic surge takes defiant stand: 'Not gonna stop'

Justin Tye told Fox News Digital he won't back down after being doxxed for speaking out about mosques and Muslim immigrants in Warren, Michigan.

Several residents in the town of Warren, Michigan are expressing concerns that their town could become the next Dearborn as the Islamic population surges.

A Michigan man who is facing backlash for speaking out against the growing Islamic population in his town refused to back down during an interview with Fox News Digital.

"This is my home, this is where I was born and raised, this city, this state," said Justin Tye, 57, of Warren, Michigan.

Tye's address was doxxed in the wake of a Fox News Digital story where he described how his town and neighborhood have been transformed by mostly Muslim immigrants over the past decade or so. He said he's received some hate mail, including a package addressed to "Justin Tye, Bigot at Large."

Justin Tye stands on his front lawn in Warren, Michigan on Aug. 25, 2026. (Peter D'Abrosca/Fox News Digital)

WORKING-CLASS AMERICANS SAY THEIR TOWN IS THE NEXT DEARBORN — AND THEY'VE HAD ENOUGH

One package contained stickers reading "F— Trump and f— you for voting for him," along with a box of feminine hygiene products.

But Tye isn't afraid of any backlash.

"Some things are worth the trouble, and this is worth the trouble that could come from it," he said. "Being doxxed, I'm not afraid. I kind of figured this was gonna come with the territory."

He also vowed to keep speaking out.

BILL MAHER RIPS IMMIGRANTS WHO REFUSE TO ADAPT, SAYS AMERICAN VALUES ARE ‘NOT NEGOTIABLE’

"I'm not gonna stop. I mean, you come here from another country and you disrespect the people who have lived in this neighborhood for decades, and in many cases like myself, there's several people I went to school with that bought their parents' homes and live back here," he said, adding that he is speaking up for his neighbors too.

A package sent to Justin Tye's home after he discussed the surging Islamic population in Warren, Michigan. (Justin Tye)

"And that's what I've been hearing mainly is, 'finally a voice,'" he said. "These people here, these Muslims ... you need to respect the people, the Americans that are here. Stop disrespecting the people that lived here for decades."

Tye said he's received encouragement from residents around town.

"I'm getting a lot of support," he said. Like I was out, I had to go do some shopping. I went to Meijer, I went to the bank, and then I stopped at a pizza place to get a pizza, and all three places I was stopped by people, asked if I was the Justin that was interviewed by Fox, and I said 'yes.' And the support I'm getting is incredible."

Tye and several of his neighbors spoke to Fox News Digital several weeks ago in Warren.

PASTOR UNLEASHES ON DEARBORN AS RELIGIOUS TENSIONS ERUPT AT CITY COUNCIL MEETING: 'ENOUGH IS ENOUGH'

"It all started when they bought the mosque, roughly six years ago," said Tye.

"After Ramadan, they would have their [Eid al-Fitr] prayer service. It was unannounced. We didn't know anything," he continued. "All of a sudden, we were just woken up to 100-plus people behind the mosque, with an imam on a podium with big amplifier speakers, belting out his prayer service. So it woke up the whole neighborhood."

TRUMP INAUGURATION PASTOR SAYS DEARBORN CHRISTIANS 'AFRAID' TO SPEAK OUT IN MUSLIM-MAJORITY CITY

He described his neighborhood now as "chaos."

He also took Fox News Digital on a guided tour of Warren, and pointed out five new mosques built or under construction within a seven-mile radius of his house.
